text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said it confirmed the ratings of Agrium Inc's senior unsecured debt at A and commercial paper at A-1, with a stable outlook.

"Agrium continues to generate strong earnings and cash flow as declining world grain stocks and increased North American acreage have increased demand for the company's fertilizer products while expansions in both the production and retail segments have also had a positive impact," CBRS said.

Agrium has also opened four retail oulets in Argentina and reduced debt leverage, as well as completed a normal course issuer bid of 3.3 million shares. Calgary-based Agrium was also given a stable outlook because world-wide demand for grains and other crops is seen growing, CBRS said.

"In this regard, the company is continuing to investigate the feasibility of building a world scale production complex in Argentina and is at earlier stages of examination into other markets in Southeast Asia and the Caribbean," CBRS said.
The company also is seen completing an expansion program during its third quarter of 1996, which will also aid earnings, it said.
